ideas.risks: Could be non-matching because many papers use examples of confidence/advantage weak learners or require tunable weak edge; if no theorem exactly matches fixed-$\beta$ risk, this route stalls.
ideas.summary: Complete a theorem-by-theorem compatibility matrix for fixed-slack-agnostic-to-weak-boosting in KMV08, Feldman, and potential-based boosters, using exact atlas conventions (binary labels, target risk form, runtime in n,1/\u03b5,\u03b4). Produce for each candidate theorem the precise weak condition required, what the wrapper can certify from $\mathrm{err}\le\mathrm{OPT}+\beta$, and whether the final guarantee is $\mathrm{OPT}+\epsilon$, $\mathrm{OPT}+\alpha+\epsilon$, or has hidden floor terms.
ideas.title: Exact oracle-compatibility theorem matrix for fixed-slack boosting papers
ideas.why_promising: The main blocker is currently a semantic mismatch. A precise matrix can decisively close positive or negative transfer claims and may reveal a single overlooked theorem that already settles the edge.

ideas.risks: Strongest lemmas may hold only for specific hypothesis classes and not distribution-free in general, yielding limited scope if not clearly separated as conditional.
ideas.summary: Prove a quantified obstruction with an explicit tuple (C,D,F): choose C and adaptive residual filter family F where $\mathrm{OPT}_C(D) \le 1/2-\gamma$ but for every wrapper rule in F, there exists a round t with $\mathrm{OPT}_C(D_t)\ge 1/2- o(1)$ and still requires additional rounds under fixed accuracy target schedules. Require explicit lower bound on wrapper failure probability and mass trajectory under distribution-free sampling.
ideas.title: Explicit (C,D,F) obstruction for adaptive-filter OPT inflation
ideas.why_promising: This directly attacks the missing lower-bound side and can settle the implication as false for natural wrappers, or at least carve a sharp boundary for when positive results are impossible.

ideas.risks: May fail if confidence intervals become too loose under adaptive stopping, and could introduce dependence on unknown class-specific parameters.
ideas.summary: Design an adaptive-round estimator for \(\gamma_t=1/2-\mathrm{OPT}_C(D_t)\): derive high-probability lower bounds from observed residual/filter statistics under stopping-time dependence. Target a PAC-SGD-style optional-stopping bound that is both computable and union-bounded over T=poly(1/\u03b5) rounds.
ideas.title: Adaptive-robust estimator of round-wise OPT gap
ideas.why_promising: The main positive route fails purely on certifiability. A validated lower-bound estimator would remove a concrete computational gate and could make a conditional invariant-based reduction formal.

ideas.risks: Could be impossible without extra assumptions; may only prove one-way or on restricted distributions; might not connect to general oracle model.
ideas.summary: Test conditional positives under structural assumptions (e.g., bounded Tsybakov/Massart noise, low noise exponent, margin conditions, or bounded-density filtering). Show that under such assumptions a wrapper can maintain both mass(D_t)\u2208poly^{-1} and \(\gamma_t\ge\mathrm{poly}^{-1}(n,1/\u03b5)\), then derive explicit boosting depth and runtime.
ideas.title: Conditionally positive theorem under noise/margin/regularity assumptions
ideas.why_promising: If successful, it gives a clean, high-precision theorem for structured settings and may suggest exactly which assumptions are missing in general instances.

ideas.risks: May require nontrivial oracle simulation reductions and could be weaker than needed for full negative separation.
ideas.summary: Model fixed-slack learner as fixed-tolerance statistical-query/online-to-batch primitive and prove lower bounds showing that for classes like parity/low-degree polynomials under well-chosen distributions, constant-specified edge queries cannot be amplified to arbitrary \u03b5 within poly time if only 0/1 predictions are returned.
ideas.title: SQ/precision-barrier formalization for fixed-slack-only oracles
ideas.why_promising: A quantitative lower bound could provide principled obstruction and explain why known boosters leave additive floors, potentially turning heuristic skepticism into theorem-level impossibility.

ideas.risks: Could be impossible if weak oracle randomness and wrapper randomness are unremovable; may still fail practical sample bounds.
ideas.summary: Construct a wrapper that converts fixed-slack excess-risk outputs into a calibrated weak edge/margin query via repeated sampling, label-dependent reweighting, or pairwise difference tricks, with explicit control on additional bias and variance. Target one-shot reduction: if wrapper returns \(\mathrm{err}\le\mathrm{OPT}+\beta\), output a hypothesis for the booster interface with guaranteed advantage function \(\gamma(\beta,\hat p)\) and polynomial overhead.
ideas.title: Calibration gadget from fixed-slack risk to explicit weak edge for existing boosters
ideas.why_promising: Many existing boosting analyses only fail due to interface mismatch; if this mapping is feasible, the rest may become largely modular.
